about.title: Monterey Park Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a fatal collision happens on a corridor like Garfield Avenue, SR-60, or Garvey Avenue, the days that follow are overwhelming. Monterey Park sees hundreds of injury collisions each year, and while recent records show no traffic deaths in the most current final count, fatal crashes and other fatal incidents still happen and leave families searching for answers. California law gives certain surviving family members the right to pursue a wrongful death claim, but the rules about who can file and how long they have are specific and unforgiving of delay. We listen to what happened, then help your family understand your legal options with clarity and care. You focus on grieving and healing; let us carry the legal weight for a while. There's no cost to you unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in Monterey Park Choose Us

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with certain dependents or heirs eligible in other situations. We can help clarify where your family fits before any claim moves forward.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, but that window shrinks significantly when a government entity is involved. Waiting to sort out details can quietly cost a family its legal options.

items.title: Losses Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance — not just medical bills. We can help make sure nothing is overlooked in a claim, separate from any related criminal case.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, California law allows two years from the date of death, though claims against a government entity — such as one involving a city-maintained road — have a much shorter deadline. Because Monterey Park corridors like SR-60 involve state and local agencies, it's worth having us review the specifics quickly.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: California law gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none of those relationships apply, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing instead. We can help sort out exactly where your family stands.

items.question: What if the fatal crash happened on a busy Monterey Park street like Garvey Avenue?
items.answer: High-traffic corridors such as Garvey Avenue, Atlantic Boulevard, and Garfield Avenue see a steady volume of collisions in Monterey Park, and public crash records can become important evidence in a claim. We can help gather and interpret those records as part of building your case.

items.question: Do you charge anything for this service?
items.answer: No. We provide wrongful death claim assistance at no cost, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
